stories.title: Lakers' Austin Reaves day-to-day with bruised heel, doesn't undergo imaging
stories.summary: The Lakers appear to have avoided serious fallout from an injury-riddled game.
stories.detailText: Any Los Angeles Lakers game in which Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves both exit with injuries is going to be concerning, but it appears the team has dodged any serious fallout. Two days after the Lakers’ two leading scorers left a win over the Milwaukee Bucks , head coach JJ Redick told reporters Friday that he expects Dončić to be available for Sunday’s game against the Phoenix Suns. Dončić had already told reporters he was “good” the night of the injury, which was a tweaked ankle. As for Reaves, Redick said the guard was day-to-day with a bruise on his heel, but the matter is apparently minor enough the team didn’t even bother with imaging on the foot. “AR, based on his physical evaluation and how he was feeling yesterday, we opted against imaging. He’ll be day-to-day. We’ll have him on the report tomorrow at 5 o’clock.“ Even with their early exits Friday, no pair of teammates is averaging more com,bined points per game than Dončić and Reaves. Dončić leads the league in scoring with 38.6 points per game, while Reaves if 15th with 24.7. Dončić is also ninth in the league in assists per game at 7.6. Rotation guard Collin Sexton also exited Friday’s game a collision with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins. He needed stitches above his right eye, but Redick said a concussion was ruled out and he’s “probably in the same boat” as Reaves. The Lakers-Suns game is scheduled for 1 p.m. PT on Sunday in Phoenix.

stories.title: Lakers' Austin Reaves day-to-day with left heel bruise
stories.summary: Lakers guard Austin Reaves is considered day-to-day as he deals with a left heel bruise, coach JJ Redick said Friday.
stories.detailText: EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves is considered day-to-day as he deals with a left heel bruise, coach JJ Redick said after practice Friday. Reaves left L.A.'s 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday midway through the third quarter and did not return after landing awkwardly on his left foot after missing a contested fast-break dunk. Reaves underwent X-rays at the arena Wednesday that came back clean. After seeing how Reaves was feeling Thursday morning once the Lakers returned to Los Angeles, the team determined that further medical imaging on the shooting guard's foot would not be necessary. When Redick was asked if Reaves had suffered only a "minor" injury, considering the Lakers decided to forgo an MRI, the coach replied: "I would assume a day-to-day injury is minor, yeah." Redick provided injury updates on three other Lakers players as well. Luka Doncic , who turned his right ankle late in the win over the Bucks, "is fine," according to Redick. "I think the expectation would be he's available," Redick said, referring to L.A.'s next game against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday. Redick said backup guard Collin Sexton , who required stitches above his right eye after he and Bucks guard Ryan Rollins unintentionally head-butted one another Wednesday, was cleared of any concussion symptoms but is also considered day-to-day. Guard Quentin Grimes , who sprained the right pinkie on his shooting hand and missed the Lakers' past two games, participated in the live portion of practice Friday, Redick said. Grimes said he jammed the finger in the Pistons game and taped it up for practice. "The swelling has gone down a lot," Grimes said. "It's kind of feeling basically back to normal." The Lakers, at 11-2, own the No. 1 record in the NBA. Redick used the three-day break in the schedule to "audit" the team. He said he had his analytics department prepare a 21-page presentation he used, along with a film session, to discuss L.A.'s defensive and offensive identities before practice Friday. "It was good," forward Ziaire Williams said of the meeting. "A lot of good things and a lot of things to clean up. Being first in the West, with the stuff that they showed us, you would think we were almost last, you know? But yeah, for sure, got to keep us honest."

stories.title: Dejounte Murray wants trade from Pelicans; both sides working on resolution
stories.summary: Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution.
stories.detailText: New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution. "Today, Dejounte Murray's representatives informed us of his request to be traded," the Pelicans said in a statement Friday. "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization." Murray has made it clear to the organization that he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. Murray has been ruled out because of a left ankle sprain for Friday night's NBA Cup game against the Memphis Grizzlies . After the latest game, Murray tweeted a response to an account that noted that the Pelicans are 3-0 without Murray in the lineup and 1-8 with him on the court: "From what's going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!," the since-deleted tweet read . Murray, 30, was acquired by the Pelicans in a June 2024 trade with the Atlanta Hawks , as New Orleans dealt two first-round picks, Dyson Daniels , Larry Nance Jr . and E.J. Liddell to Atlanta for him. Murray was coming off a 2023-24 season in which he averaged 22.5 points, 6.4 assists and 5.3 rebounds per game. He has dealt with major injuries and played just 54 games over the past three seasons, however. He has averaged 16.6 points, 6.6 assists and 5.9 rebounds for the Pelicans, shooting just 41.9% from the floor. He broke a hand in the 2024 season opener and suffered a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon in January 2025. Murray is averaging just 13.4 points per game this season. Murray, who made the All-Star team in 2022, is making $32.8 million this season and has a player option for $30.8 million next season.

stories.title: Why failure without Kawhi Leonard is ok, but not without Scottie Barnes
stories.summary: Failure can be a good teacher, but repeating old lessons only helps so much
stories.detailText: TORONTO, ON- OCTOBER 21 - Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard #2 of the Toronto Raptors share a laugh on the bench as the Toronto Raptors play the Chicago Bulls in their season opener at Scotiabank Arena in Toronto. October 21, 2026. Steve Russell/Toronto Star (Steve Russell/Toronto Star via Getty Images) | Toronto Star via Getty Images When you start dating, there’s something to be said for bad dates and breakups serving as lessons for the do’s and don’ts of the world of romance. But, if you keep making the same crummy jokes, not brushing your teeth, over and over again, you’re not learning much from those bad dates. At a certain point, losing becomes unproductive. It’s kind of like that with basketball, too. And in the last couple of matches, the Toronto Raptors’ losing has been real, real unproductive. Because, it doesn’t tell anyone anything that they don’t already know. TORONTO, ON- OCTOBER 21 – Scottie Barnes #4 of the Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard #2 of the Toronto Raptors share a laugh on the bench as the Toronto Raptors play the Chicago Bulls in their season opener at Scotiabank Arena in Toronto. October 21, 2026. Steve Russell/Toronto Star (Steve Russell/Toronto Star via Getty Images) | Toronto Star via Getty Images Both times when the Raptors have traded for Kawhi Leonard, there’s been an implicit gamble attached to that. Leonard won’t play a lot of regular season games, but take him to the playoffs okay, and he’ll turn into the ‘84 Terminator, or ‘85 Jordan, whichever set of skills might be needed more that night. This season, Kawhi went out early. Okay. That just means that the other guys need to start pulling extra weight a little sooner. And you remember the playoff series against the Cavaliers, and say, “okay, Scottie and RJ, maybe they can anchor this offence, even without a scorer like Brandon Ingram or Kawhi Leonard.” And then… Scottie Barnes goes down. Yikes. An old teacher of mine told me that “practice doesn’t make perfect — perfect practice makes perfect,” and it concerns me that that Raptors are just practicing really, far, far away from perfect. Now, Scottie seems like he’s going to come back soon; when exactly that will be is unclear, but there has been little indication that the groin strain is something particularly serious. But, losing the games that the Raptors are losing, without Scottie Barnes, doesn’t really help them understand how their team is going to perform in playoff settings, which, for this roster, should be the ultimate goal. Before the season started, Bobby Webster spoke to the media, and argued that the question that should remain pervasive throughout the season should be “ can we win every night ?” Toronto Raptors regular season record without Kawhi Leonard. 2018-‘19: 17-5 2026-‘27: 3-6 The Raptors now have more losses without Kawhi in his 2nd stint than his 1st stint. It’s still November, and we still don’t know when Kawhi is back from injury this season, and, God… pic.twitter.com/g25BAtaNjZ — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) November 12, 2026 Thus far, the answer to that question, without Kawhi Leonard, has be a resounding “no.” Omer Osman illustrates that clearly, in the tweet above. It’s not 2019 anymore. The Raptors are a different beast, younger, less veteran-heavy, and constructed in a less careful manner. With Scottie missing the last couple of matchups against heavy-hitters like Boston and Philadelphia, the Raptors don’t know how well the team can operate in an optimal sans-Kawhi state, because Toronto was never expecting to, and is not built to, compete without both of its All-Stars. Barnes was showcasing that he’s taken a leap offensively, and can piggy-back the Raptors — to a degree — but when facing off against diminished rosters of great teams, and the forward isn’t there to help the Raptors take advantage of weakened clubs, the Raptors are effectively leaving both wins or positive reps on the table, and without Barnes, aren’t necessarily getting either. This isn’t to say that there’s *zero* value from playing without Barnes or Leonard. RJ Barrett just had a season high in points, and is continuing to prove his value. Jakob Poeltl has quietly been looking more like his uninjured self again. And the team’s younger players are getting more time on the court to find their legs and develop themselves further. But, this season was never meant to be about development. It was meant to be about the Raptors bashing teams’ heads in with lockdown defence and gliding to the playoffs. But, ultimately, the team has to play the cards they’re dealt. The season thus far hasn’t been the triumphant return of Raptors basketball to the big stage anyone expected, but there’s a lot of basketball left in the year. @BAAILEYYCREATES on Twitter raised an important point; that last year, Leonard’s health management kept him off the court almost entirely until the new year, and when he was back, he was whooping teams left right and centre. It’s not 2019 anymore, and Kawhi is 35 years old now, but that means, simply, that ramping up looks different for Leonard now, not that he’s unable to deliver on-court product. The Raptors need to be able to compete with and without Leonard for this roster to work, but without Scottie Barnes to lead the charge, Toronto will remain in dire straits.

stories.title: Dejounte Murray requests trade from Pelicans
stories.summary: Friday's news comes on the heels of the Pelicans' blowout losses to the Warriors and Nets.
stories.detailText: After two-plus seasons, Dejounte Murray's time in New Orleans may be coming to a close. ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday that the veteran point guard has requested a trade, with the Pelicans confirming the news shortly thereafter. This comes on the heels of two blowout defeats for the Pelicans: a 51-point thrashing by the Warriors on Monday, followed by a 34-point loss to the Nets on Wednesday. In their statement, the Pelicans said that they will "evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization." Murray has appeared in nine games this season, averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.6 steals in 31.4 minutes per game. He's started alongside second-year guard Jeremiah Fears, whom many view as the Pelicans' point guard of the future. Murray missed three games in late October/early November for personal reasons, and the Pelicans won all three, with Fears flourishing and Herb Jones providing quality defensive play as the replacement in the starting lineup. In a since-deleted social media post, Murray responded to a post noting the Pelicans' record in the games he missed, saying, "From what's going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this! THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!" Acquired from the Hawks during the 2024 offseason, Murray has appeared in 54 games for the Pelicans over two-plus seasons. His 2024-25 campaign was cut short by an Achilles tendon rupture, which also sidelined him for most of the 2025-26 season. He had already been ruled out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies with an ankle injury by the time reports of a trade request surfaced.

stories.title: Lakers provide Austin Reaves injury update. Will star guard miss games?
stories.summary: Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick provided an injury update on Austin Reaves after the guard landed awkwardly on his left heel.
stories.detailText: Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick provided an injury update on shooting guard Austin Reaves . Redick stated during his Friday, Nov. 13 media availability that Reaves suffered a bruised heel and is considered day-to-day. The coach added that Reaves and the team's medical staff opted against having imaging done on the injury. Reaves had landed awkwardly on his left heel after missing a transition dunk attempt in the middle of the third quarter of the Lakers' 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 11. After feeling some discomfort, he limped back to the locker room. The initial X-rays taken at the arena were negative, and Redick ruled out any potential Achilles tendon damage. Reaves was one of several injury scares suffered during the game against the Bucks. Luka Dončić avoided a severe injury after turning his right ankle in the same game. Collin Sexton also needed stitches above his right eye after bumping heads with Ryan Rollins of the Bucks. Dončić: Lakers star 'feeling good' after injury scare Reaves has played in 12 of 13 game for the Lakers this season, starting in all 12 of those contests. He is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebound, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting 51.3% from the field and 40.9% from beyond the arc. When do Lakers play next? Reaves and the Lakers will have more time to rest before traveling to Phoenix to take on the Suns at 4 p.m. ET (2 p.m. local) on Sunday, Nov. 15. stories.title: Lakers' Austin Reaves considered day-to-day with heel injury
stories.summary: The team opted not to have Reaves undergo more imaging. Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes are also day-to-day, while Luka Doncic is expected to play Sunday at Phoenix.
stories.detailText: Lakers guard Austin Reaves, getting poked in the face by Heat guard Pelle Larsson during a game this month, is considered day-to-day after injuring his left heel during a game in Milwaukee. (Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times) On the day the Lakers hosted their annual Thanksgiving Feast event to kick off their “ Season of Giving ” at the team’s practice facility, they were able to give some thanks for dodging serious injuries. Austin Reaves didn’t have to get further imaging on his injured left heel, coach JJ Redick said after practice Friday, and the star guard will be listed as day-to-day for Sunday’s game at Phoenix. Redick also said that All-Star guard Luka Doncic was “fine” after injuring his ankle in a win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night, that a concussion was ruled out for guard Collin Sexton after he received stitches to his forehead following a collision with Milwaukee’s Ryan Rollins, and that guard Quentin Grimes worked out in the stay-ready-game against coaches after missing two games because of a finger injury. Reaves left Wednesday’s win in the third quarter and didn’t return. His X-rays after the game were negative and by Thursday morning, when the team had returned to L.A. after winning the first three of the four-game trip, Reaves felt well enough that he and team personnel opted against getting more imaging. Redick said Reaves has a bruise on his heel and described it as “minor.” Read more: 'It's forever': Lakers rookie Cameron Carr cherishing first NBA points Doncic, who leads the NBA in scoring (38.6 points) and is ninth in assists (7.6), is doing OK after he injured his right ankle in the fourth quarter Wednesday. “The expectation would be he’s available,” Redick said. Sexton had to get stitches above his right eye after the collision with 6:51 left in the fourth quarter Wednesday. Redick said Sexton also will be day-to-day. Lakers guard Collin Sexton, preparing to defend Hawks guard Kingston Flemings, is listed as day-to-day after getting stitches above his right eye following a collision during a win over the Bucks. (Mike Stewart / Associated Press) Grimes, who missed two games because of a sprained finger on his right hand, participated in the live portion of the stay-ready game Wednesday and expects to play Sunday. Grimes wore a wrap on his right pinky finger while speaking with reporters. “I had a really good day just playing with a little tape over it,” Grimes said. “Just seeing how it felt the first time, but it felt really good. We got a lot of wins out there in them games, at least. But it felt really good out there.” The Lakers will have three days off before they play again Sunday to Phoenix. Even though the Lakers have the best record in the NBA (11-2), are the top scoring team (122.2 points) in the league and rank first in offensive rating (121.6), Redick wanted to let his group know there is room for improvement. During the film session Friday he told his team they “were 17th in defense” rating at 113.6. And the Lakers are 27th in rebounding. Redick said he and his staff talked about “20 things” that they can clean up. “We filtered through our offensive stuff based on our identities of who we want to be offensively: organized, unselfish and advantage-based,” Redick said. “Then we went through the stats on that. “Then we went to our defense and our three identities: organized, physical as hell and relentless. And we went through the stats on those things. So, it’s a very clean thing. We’ve done that for the last 2½ seasons. It’s just everything that we present to the team lines up with who we’re trying to be.” Redick got his message through to his players. “Being first in the West, with the stuff that they showed us, you would think we were almost last, you know?” forward Ziaire Williams said. “But it’s gotta keep us honest. But you know, it’s good to know that there’s still room for growth as good as we’re doing. So yeah, it was great, it was great. So yeah, hopefully we’ll clean that up going into the next game against Phoenix.” Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.summary: With Dejounte Murray reportedly seeking a trade, the Suns could have an opportunity to turn Jalen Green into a better fit.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 09: Dejounte Murray #5 of the New Orleans Pelicans reacts during a break in play in the third quarter against the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center on November 09, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the first eleven games of the season, it has not all been sunshine and rainbows for this Suns team. They have seen injuries, rebounding issues, and lapses on both ends of the floor. This has brought them to a 5-6 record, which lets them beat the bad teams but struggle against the good ones. As Espo from PHNX said the other night, they are basically in basketball purgatory right now, and some things need to change. Regardless of whether it’s a lineup switch, plugging in Jordan Goodwin or Collin Gillespie for Jalen Green, or potentially a trade on the horizon. Devin Booker showed up and show d out but the win left something to be desired. pic.twitter.com/YUvk3gYjXM — Espo  (@Espo) November 13, 2026 In last night’s contest against the Charlotte Hornets, we saw Jalen Green benched and not finish the game. This move allowed the Suns to regain their lead and still win a game they should have controlled the whole way. Since Green hasn’t been playing well in the lineup and has been forced into this playmaking role, many are making him the scapegoat for the team’s early-season struggles. While they are right to put most of the blame on him, it is not entirely his fault, as sometimes the bigs have trouble rebounding or some of the forwards are not locked in defensively. No Green, no Bridges in the clutch. That’s saying something, isn’t it? — John Voita, III (@DarthVoita) November 13, 2026 This is where Green has become a devalued asset across the league, as they now know he cannot fit with this starting lineup, and the Suns will likely switch things up as we get closer to the deadline. With Green still 24, some lottery teams will likely be willing to take a chance on him and let him shine with their club. For the Suns, today’s news may have made that landing spot clearer. Dejounte Murray of the New Orleans Pelicans has requested a trade. I’ve highlighted him multiple times as a good target for the Suns for many reasons, but now that his value is depleted and he’s on the market, this is the perfect trade for both teams. Both teams have an asset with depreciated value that could help the other franchise, and everyone seems to be catching on. New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul and team officials have started working on a resolution for the one-time All-Star, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/OoozAwcqvN — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) November 13, 2026 They’ve also been linked to Murray via Chris Haynes in this tweet. Haynes was the first to address locker-room concerns via the Suns, saying many felt the team needed a true point guard. Well, Murray could come in and fill that role as a better fit for the starters, but also mesh into the defensive identity that Jordan Ott wants to bring to this Phoenix team, The Phoenix Suns have registered interest in New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray who has let it be known that he seeks a change of scenery, league sources tell me. — Chris Haynes (@ChrisBHaynes) November 13, 2026 Murray, who has a $30.8 million player option next season, would accept it heading into next offseason but at 30, doesn’t seem to want a long-term, expensive deal. On the other hand, Green is young and looking to extend long term. With Booker’s contract coming up, plus the Brooks extension and a potential Bridges extension, and Beal’s dead money, it doesn’t seem feasible to pay all four players, especially when they look this bad on the court together. Green is also the same player option as Murray, just at $36 million, and is making that same amount this season, so not only would you save $4 million this season and $6 million next year, but you would save yourself from a pain-inducing contract negotiation. It is clear Green can’t be a starter given his recent play, and Murray, who has been a head case in NOLA, may be the same, but it’s an unknown. I feel Murray, who has been frustrated with the Pelicans this season, will buy into the Suns’ culture once he gets here. As we know, the Pelicans are bad and lack a clear direction for building. They view Herb Jones and Trey Murphy III as high pieces but not the building blocks of their rebuild. It seems like there are three timelines: Jones and Murphy III, Zion Williamson, and Murray as the vets who can help with a playoff push, and then you’ve got Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen as the young building blocks. Getting a young player like Green may not be the best fit, but it would give him a chance to return to his scoring form and try to become their number-one offensive option. Dejounte Murray called Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley a bitch after he hit a three 🍿 (h/t @BuiltinDaBoot ) pic.twitter.com/dDmA6rvguj — Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) November 12, 2026 For the Suns, this move frees up some money and gives you a player who can hopefully buy into the culture and help alleviate some of the pain for your best player. Murray isn’t coming in as a game-changing secondary option, but if he can buy into the team role and do the little things, he could find some great success in this starting lineup. Murray was an all-caliber defender in San Antonio, and yeah, he’s had many injuries, but I still think some of that player is still in him if he gets to Phoenix. Ultimately, time will tell whether the Suns make this move or switch their starting lineups first. One good thing to know, though, is that Murray wants out, and the Suns look like one of the only teams that would need a true point guard. With both Green and Murray at their lowest values and on similar contracts, it seems a one-for-one deal could be the easiest thing for both parties. That said, the Pelicans front office doesn’t have the best track record with trades, so maybe the Suns can get something else thrown in for taking on their disgruntled player, since Green hasn’t made his frustrations as obvious as Murray’s. Could the Suns try to get a pick back in exchange for a younger asset? That’s something I’d like to see them try to pull off, alongside bringing in Murray to give them more flexibility in the long term. Dejounte Murray has "strong interest" in joining the Phoenix Suns, per @sam_amick His camp has been hopeful for a swap involving Jalen Green, but team sources on both sides recently said no talks had taken place. pic.twitter.com/z5BlT2vPK2 — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 13, 2026 What are your thoughts? Is Dejounte Murray someone you would like the Suns to go after? Is there another piece you think would be a better fit? Ultimately, given what assets the Suns have to trade, this may be the best option they can pursue without hurting their depth too much, and I’d like it to materialize.

stories.title: Lakers get lucky with Austin Reaves’ injury update
stories.summary: Austin Reaves’ injury update wasn’t as dire as it could’ve been.
stories.detailText: Austin Reaves’ injury update wasn’t as dire as it could’ve been. Lakers coach JJ Redick said Reaves has a bruised left heel. Reaves had X-rays after Wednesday’s win over the Bucks which were negative. Reaves and the Lakers’ medical staff determined no further imaging was needed after seeing how Reaves felt Thursday morning. Reaves is day-to-day, according to Redick. Austin Reaves shouldn’t be sidelined for long. NBAE via Getty Images While it’s unclear whether Reaves will be available when the Lakers play the Suns on Sunday, Friday’s news was a sigh of relief for the franchise. Austin Reaves suffered a heel injury during the second half of the Lakers’ win over the Bucks on Wednesday. AP Photo/Aaron Gash Reaves subbed himself out and limped to the back of Fiserv Forum with team personnel because of the heel injury he suffered midway through the third quarter of the Lakers’ eventual seventh straight victory of the season . He motioned to the bench around the 5:20 mark of the quarter for him to come out of the game, with the Lakers making multiple subs while Reaves walked to the back. The Lakers ruled Reaves out for the remainder of the game midway through the fourth quarter, saying he had a heel injury. Austin Reaves’ hot start to the season hit a hitch with his heel injury. NBAE via Getty Images Reaves recorded 18 points, five assists, three rebounds and three steals in 25 minutes before leaving the game. The 6-foot-5 guard entered Wednesday as the league’s No. 15 scorer, averaging 25.3 points (50.8% from the field, 41.3% on 3-pointers), 4.6 assists and 3.4 rebounds in the team’s first nine games. Among players averaging at least 20 points per game, Reaves and Warriors star Steph Curry were the only ones to reach that scoring threshold while also shooting at least 50% from the field, 40% on 3-pointers and 90% on free throws.

stories.title: The Goal of the Utah Jazz This Season: Win The NBA Cup
stories.summary: They say that I’m a dreamer.
stories.detailText: I love the NBA Cup #nba #NBACup pic.twitter.com/ZYapVfIUKX — Roundball Renaissance (@_roundball) October 31, 2026 If you follow me on TikTok or Twitter you may already know this about me, but for those who don’t: I am a BIG NBA Cup supporter. We #RespectTheCup in this house. I am also a big soccer (or as I call it, footy) fan, so I was already prone to enjoying these in-season tournaments. When it was announced I actually think that I was one of the only ones in my content creation circle, and certainly the only one in my friend group, to be 100% on board with the idea. While Adam Silver has had more missteps in the last few years than I would prefer, he knocked it out of the park with the NBA Cup. As mentioned above, I think that there are ways to improve the tournament, but even in its short existence, it has brought much needed excitement and punch to the early portion of the NBA season. The Utah Jazz haven’t had the season that any of us would have envisioned, and while starting 1-11 is quite the hole to put ourselves in, the NBA Cup allows us to strive towards a real goal outside of “development.” Even more important than presenting an opportunity to lift up some hardware, getting all the way to the NBA Cup Final would prove that this team is ready to compete one day. The NBA Cup’s lineage is relatively short, but in its brief history we’ve been able to see some truly great basketball teams compete for the prize. If we take a trip down memory lane, we will notice something almost immediately — the teams that make it are/were threats to the rest of the league. These weren’t flukes, they were mistakes; if you made it to the Final, you were a team with the aspirations and the roster to play basketball in June. 2023-2024 The inaugural NBA Cup Final was a success by every single metric there is. The game drew 4.58 million viewers between ABC and ESPN, the arena in Las Vegas hosted over 19,000 fans, and the Final featured one of the most exciting teams in the league at the time in the Indiana Pacers and the one of the most well known brands in all of sports in the Los Angeles Lakers, of course led by LeBron James – one of the most recognizable athletes in the world. While the Lakers weren’t world beaters at this time, being three years removed from a championship, the year prior this squad lost in the Western Conference Finals to the ever dangerous Denver Nuggets. On the other side of the bracket, Tyrese Haliburton and the Indiana Pacers were the talk of the town. Haliburton was coming off of an All-Star campaign the year prior and the Pacers were just so fun to watch. The matchup also presented an opportunity for there to be a “passing of the torch” moment, but LeBron had other plans. LeBron finished the game with 24 points, 11 rebounds, and 4 assists, Anthony Davis had a game of a lifetime with 41 points and 20 rebounds, and Austin Reaves chipped in 28 points off the bench in route to a 123-109 victory. LeBron won the inaugural NBA Cup MVP award, the most recognizable NBA team in the world won the inaugural NBA Cup, and the win reiterated that the Los Angeles Lakers were still going to compete at the highest level. While I was personally rooting for the Indiana Pacers in this game, they gave it everything they had. Haliburton had a cool 20 point and 11 assist performance while Bennedict Mathurin scored 20 off the bench. It wasn’t the result that they (or I) wanted, but it wasn’t long before they proved to be worthy opponents themselves. Lest we forget that the Pacers could have been one catastrophic injury away from lifting up the Larry O’Brien Trophy the following year in the 2024-2025 NBA Season. 2024-2025 The second iteration of the NBA Cup had quite the shoes to fill, but the NBA Cup Final did not disappoint. While there wasn’t a widely recognizable brand in the Final like the Lakers or the Celtics, there was a massive amount of star power. The Milwaukee Bucks were just a few years removed from a NBA Championship themselves, and Giannis Antetokounmpo was out to prove that they could still compete. Giannis was, and still is, one of the the world’s best players and one of the game’s biggest names. With Damian Lillard at his side, Giannis was out to prove that the Bucks were still threats to come out of the East. Over in the West, the Oklahoma City Thunder were taking the league by storm. The year prior the team showed up on everyone’s radar after winning 57 games, and this year turned out to be no different. After it was all said and done, the OKC Thunder won 68 games led by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander who won his first MVP award, and the crew hoisted the Larry O’Brien Trophy at the end of the year. Unfortunately for the Thunder, Giannis and the Bucks weren’t ready to lose this night. Giannis lead the way with a 26 point, 19 rebound, and 10 assist triple-double while Damian Lillard scored 23 points and led the Bucks to a 97-81 victory. The Power of Friendship didn’t help the Thunder on this night, but they did give it their best effort: SGA scored 21, Jalen Williams scored 18,and Isaiah Hartenstein chipped in 16. While they weren’t victorious this night, they did prove to the world that they could compete with anyone in the league. After making it all the way to the NBA Cup Final, they dominated the regular season and defeated the aforementioned Indiana Pacers in 7 games in the NBA Finals. 2025-2026 The third iteration of the NBA Cup was arguably the best of the three. It also combined the best of both worlds from the previous two matchups: mega star power AND a recognizable brand. The New York Knicks are either the second or third (depending on who you ask) most recognizable brand in all of basketball, and for good reason. They don’t call Madison Square Garden “The Mecca of Basketball” for no reason. To top it all off, the Knicks were coming off of a 51 win season and a Conference Finals appearance the previous year, and Jalen Brunson just made the All-NBA 2nd Team. Out west the San Antonio Spurs were well ahead of schedule with their roster. Stephon Castle just won the Rookie of the Year award the previous year, they drafted Dylan Harper with the #2 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, and Victor Wembanyama had displayed All-World potential despite missing most of the 2024-2025 NBA season with DVT. To a lesser extent compared to the Knicks, the Spurs are also a world wide brand in the basketball realm due to the success of international stars like Tony Parker and Manu Ginobili. With all of the star power and recognizable brands at play, it shouldn’t be a surprise that the Amazon Prime Video broadcast averaged over 3 million viewers. What also wasn’t a surprise is that both teams came to play. The Spurs had 7 players in double figures; Wemby and Dylan Harper combined for 39 points off the bench, while Stephon Castle scored 15 points and dropped 12 dimes as a starter. For the Knicks, their Power of Friendship mantra rang true with 7 players scoring in double digits led by Jalen Brunson’s 25 points and OG Anunoby’s 28 points. The Knicks came out on top 124-113, but this was just the appetizer for the NBA Finals. In the NBA Cup Final both teams proved that they had what it took to compete at the highest level, and then they both powered their way through the NBA Playoffs to meet in the NBA Finals. Unfortunately for The Baseline Bums , the Knicks prevailed again in a 4-1 series win to secure a championship for the first time in 53 years. Time and time again, the NBA Cup has proven to be the battleground for future competitors and NBA Championship threats. In all three years of existence, the teams competing in the NBA Cup have either already climbed to the mountain top or they were getting ready to take the league by storm. THAT is what we should be striving for. I think after the 1-11 start it would be very difficult to compete for a Playoff spot (I predicted that we would finish 7th) so we should strive to do something more enticing than another year of developing our young talent. We had higher expectations for our team, but we’ve had a season from hell when it comes to the injury department: Jaren Jackson Jr. is out until the new year, Jusuf Nurkic will be out for at least another two weeks, and Lauri Markkanen will miss at least a month with his hand fracture. Do I think that it will be difficult to win the games necessary to advance in the NBA Cup tournament without them? Absolutely. Do I think that this is a tremendous chance for our young players to prove what they can do? Without a doubt. The road will be hard, especially after dropping our first NBA Cup game against the Mavericks 112-100, but I don’t think that our chance to win has been snuffed out. Tonight we play the Houston Rockets, and while they are formidable, they are not unbeatable. After that, the Suns and Nuggets are both very volatile. There is a real scenario where the Jazz go 3-1 in group play and earn a spot in the NBA Cup Quarter Finals. Once we get there, it just takes a hot streak to take us all the way to the Promised Land. Again, without Lauri or JJJ, the burden will be placed on our younger players and luckily we have the firepower to do it. Keyonte George is good for 20 points a game this year, Darryn Peterson became the first teenager in Utah Jazz history to score 20+ points in four straight games, and Ace Bailey has proven that he is invaluable to this team. The season has been disappointing so far, but there are reasons to be excited and goals to strive for. There is a lot of basketball left to play this year, and I for one am not satisfied with chalking up this year to another development year. Our goal for the rest of the year should be to win the NBA Cup, because if we can do that with a depleted roster, just imagine what we can do in the 2027-2028 season with a fully heathy squad. How do you feel about the NBA Cup? How do you think the Jazz will fare the rest of the season? Sound off in the comments below! Be kind. Tell somebody you love them.

stories.title: James Harden is foundational to the Cavs’ Success
stories.summary: Harden is key to anything the Cavs want to do this season.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NY - NOVEMBER 11: James Harden #1 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks on during the game against the New York Knicks on November 11, 2026 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images James Harden arrived to the Cleveland Cavaliers as a divisive figure. As the centerpiece of a trade that sent fan favorite Darius Garland to the Clippers, Harden was always going to face an uphill battle. Now, coming off an Eastern Conference Finals appearance, all eyes are on Harden as he begins his second season with the team. After twelve games, one thing is clear: his performance will determine whether the Cavaliers can improve on last year. The vibes around Harden hit a low point after Cleveland was walloped by the Charlotte Hornets, 124-112 , on November 9. He was at the center of the team’s problems. There were long stretches of minimal effort on defense, and he often looked like he was coasting, barely attempting to bring down rebounds. Offensively, it was just as bleak: 11 points on 3-9 shooting with four turnovers. Safe to say, the fanbase was ready to drive Harden to the airport and send him to whatever team, or country, would take him. Then came the Knicks game on November 11. Suddenly, Harden was energized and putting his mark on the game. He orchestrated a 115-107 road win at Madison Square Garden and put the offense on his back with 32 points, going 9-for-14 from the field with five threes and 9-11 at the free throw line. Putting those two games back to back is as stark as it is telling of where the Cavaliers are. The team knew the risks and still entered the James Harden business. This isn’t MVP Harden, and this isn’t the Houston Rockets of the 2010s, but the sentiment still stands: Cleveland is reliant on Harden to make the pieces on this roster gel. When he is at his worst, the ripples spread throughout the entire lineup. The numbers show just how much his play matters, if not in the way Cleveland hoped. Through his first 11 games, the Cavaliers had a -5.6 net rating with Harden on the floor and a +15.7 net rating with him off it. Whatever his Knicks performance does to those numbers, it was a long way from enough to erase them. Is this too much to ask of a 37-year-old? Yes. But the Cavaliers knew this was the route they were taking when they traded for Harden and then extended him on a three-year, $97 million deal. At times this season, it has looked like a grave mistake. Harden is posting some of the lowest numbers of his career: 16.7 points, 5.6 assists and 4.6 rebounds per game. That scoring is about seven points below his 23.6 average last season, and about four below the 20.5 he averaged in 26 games after joining Cleveland. His assists are down more than two per game from last season’s 8.0. Still, the Knicks game suggests the player fans expect isn’t gone. The problem for the Cavaliers is how to keep Harden engaged and empowered enough that performances like that don’t become few and far between. It will be a balancing act. Cleveland has to meet Harden at a level of comfort that lets him use his best traits, while melding his heliocentric style with an offense that fits the rest of the roster and lets the ball move more freely. That will take time. The Cavaliers knew this came with Harden, and fans need to understand it won’t be pretty until a resolution is found on the court.

The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders. Nov. 13 Murray, Pelicans working toward trade New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania. Murray has made it clear he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere. The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. From Bobby Marks: Murray signed a four-year $114 million extension with Atlanta in July 2023 but was traded the following offseason to New Orleans. He has two years remaining on his contract -- $32.8 and $30.8 million, respectively, with a player option in the second year. One salary-cap nugget a team interested in Murray will have to consider is the $2.4 million in unlikely bonuses. While he did not reach any of the incentives in the previous season, unlikely bonuses are applied to the first and second apron. With Murray on their books, New Orleans is $4 million below the luxury tax and $5.7 million under the first apron hard cap. Despite five players (including the $44.9 million nonguaranteed contract of Zion Williamson ) earning more than $21 million in 2027-28, New Orleans is well positioned below the luxury tax and apron. After not having a first-round pick in the 2026 draft, New Orleans could have two picks in the top four in 2027 -- its own and Milwaukee's. If one of those picks falls between Nos. 5 and 30, the least favorable would go to Atlanta. Brown confronted Tatum at a dinner in France about their future as teammates, per Charania. The former teammates will meet for the first time Tuesday night, as the Celtics head to Philadelphia (8 p.m. ET). NBA Trade Lab updates: How could the Lakers level up? The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric . Their projected win total from ESPN's Basketball Power Index that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing LeBron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers , but their newly added pieces have jelled together quickly to leave fans around the league rethinking what the ceiling of this team could be. After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade , the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. However, this hasn't stopped Lakers fans from diving into our NBA Trade Lab tool to cook up some mock trades in an attempt to find the Lakers another piece around the margins that could complete this roster for a deep playoff run. Trade No. 1: Lakers bring in Luka's former teammate Lakers get: P.J. Washington Dallas Mavericks get: Jarred Vanderbilt , Cameron Carr , and two second-round picks Washington is a versatile two-way wing who started alongside Doncic during the Mavericks' run to the finals in 2024. With Draymond and Steph Curry on the floor together, it was still plus-105 last year, still a good offensive rating,117.7, but the moment Steph's been off the floor, and last year he was off the floor a lot, their offense cratered when Draymond was on the floor and was actually OK when it was no Draymond and no Steph. "I've had these conversations with Steve [Kerr] and again I think you're going to hear it a lot publicly in their messaging, they're going to adapt the offense at times away from Draymond. They're going to try to make him more of a spot-up shooter at times instead of giving him the ball. They're trying to limit his turnovers." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 1 Duren, Pistons end standoff with long-term deal All-NBA center Jalen Duren has agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons , his agent told ESPN's Shams Charania. Duren had until 11:59 p.m. ET Thursday to decide on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan. "I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year." Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4). Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games. A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder , after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season. Sept. 30 Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived. Sept. 29 Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost. The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN. Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal? On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns ' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks . "Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable." Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30. Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday. "He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see." After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries. He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona , who is dealing with a sprained left foot. Anfernee Simons , who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp. "Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that." Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season. Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise. "With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right? "But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp. "He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up. Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Pelicans evaluating possibilities after trade request from Dejounte Murray, who recently rebutted criticism on social media
stories.summary: Murray is currently in his third season with the team.
stories.detailText: The New Orleans Pelicans are evaluating potential trade opportunities for Dejounte Murray after a trade request from the All-Star guard, the team announced Friday . The news comes the same week the 30-year-old Murray rebutted criticism on social media with since-deleted posts, one of which reportedly featured profanity. The Pelicans are 4-8 this season, including 1-8 in the games Murray has appeared in. Murray won't play in Friday night's NBA Cup group-play game between New Orleans and the Memphis Grizzlies, the Pelicans announced, citing his left ankle sprain . His agent Rich Paul and Pelicans officials were reported by ESPN’s Shams Charania to be working on a resolution earlier in the day. New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul and team officials have started working on a resolution for the one-time All-Star, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/OoozAwcqvN — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) November 13, 2026 The Phoenix Suns have expressed interest in the 2022 All-Star, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes. The 2026-27 campaign is his third with the Pelicans, with whom he's currently averaging 13.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.6 steals per game. That said, Murray is shooting just 29.6% from 3, and he's committed four turnovers twice so far. In the fallout of a 145-111 home loss to the 3-8 Brooklyn Nets, the X account for Pro Pels Talk, a Pelicans podcast, posted an array of game clips, breaking down the game film without mincing words. The commentary that accompanied some of those clips questioned Murray's on-court effort . As reported by The Athletic , Murray responded to one of those posts, which showcased footage of him apparently misplacing a pass intended for forward Saddiq Bey. The ball ended up low and away, resulting in a turnover, whereas Bey seemed to be asking for it near chest level. And then follows it up with this. Look at where Saddiq is calling for the basketball. Before that, Murray engaged with an NBACentral X post that noted how the Pelicans are 3-0 without him this season. Dejounte Murray just tweeted and deleted this 🤔 pic.twitter.com/rSAqV6Iepd — Ahmed/The Ears/IG: BigBizTheGod 🇸🇴 (@big_business_) November 12, 2026 On Friday, he apparently reposted Charania's report about him wanting out of New Orleans.
