stories.summary: Drew Lock was limited in practice Friday, his sixth consecutive practice without team drills.
stories.detailText: Drew Lock was limited in practice Friday, his sixth consecutive practice without team drills. Like last week, though, Lock will play through oblique and elbow injuries. Lock does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders. "He had a similar cadence and workload in terms of last week," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Friday, via John Boyle of the team website. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape." The Seahawks ruled out starter Sam Darnold (ribs/quad) for another week, but he would return after the Week 11 bye. Offensive guard Quenton Nelson (knee), offensive tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) also won't play. The Seahawks are getting back outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu, receiver Rashid Shaheed and nose tackle Brandon Pili. All three were full participants Friday and do not have an injury designation.

stories.title: 49ers-Cowboys preview: Christian McCaffrey and the Niners should run wild
stories.summary: What to expect when the 49ers have the ball, and why the defense likely only needs a few stops against the Cowboys
stories.detailText: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images History will lead you in the right direction more often than not. The head-to-head matchups between the San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys have been one-sided. It’s why it’s a rivalry in name only. How the 49ers have fared against the NFC East and the Cowboys versus the NFC West is more evidence of what to expect this coming Sunday. The Niners have been terrific in that regard, while Dallas has gone 2-5 in their previous seven games — including a loss to the Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew-led Cardinals, in a game in which they allowed 30 points. Let’s preview Week 10’s matchup to see whether Dak Prescott can keep pace with Brock Purdy. What to expect when the 49ers have the ball Purdy is 3-0 in his career against the Cowboys. His fourth start against Dallas might be the biggest mismatch, at least on this side of the ball, to date. The 49ers are top-three offensively in points per game, EPA per pass, EPA per rush, passing and rushing success rate, and in third-down and red-zone efficiency. Conversely, the Cowboys are bottom-five or worst in total yards and rushing yards per game, EPA per play and rush, sacks per game, and third-down efficiency. Dallas’s saving grace on this side of the ball is that they are sixth in turnover EPA per game. Down-to-down, they’ve been lousy. The Cowboys give up a league-high 35.2 yards per opponent possession. After a mid-season quarterback change, Arizona had drives of 70, 80, 58, and 90 yards before a 44-yard game-winning field goal drive in overtime. Atrocious against the run inside Quinnen Williams is one of the NFL’s best interior linemen. He’s the ultimate disruptor. Williams leads all defensive tackles with 14 tackles for loss—five more than Jeffery Simmons. His five sacks are tied for third. The 18 run stops are tied for third. Yet, for whatever reason, the Cowboys have been abysmal against the inside run. When you watch them, the issues stem from getting moved at the point of attack. Ball carriers aren’t getting touched until they cross the line of scrimmage. The eye test matches the stats: Dallas allows the second-most yards before contact per carry this season, at 1.78 yards. They get moved, easily, despite having played only two offenses in the top-15 in rushing success rate. The 49ers are running more and more inside the tackles. They’re running inside zone at a 19.1% clip, a slight increase from a year ago. This game sets up well for the Niners to keep attacking the Cowboys’ A and B gaps. Kyle Shanahan had to be grinning as he watched the 36-play reel of the Cowboys’ defense defending —a term used loosely—inside zone. They allowed 8.08 yards per carry. Seven of those 36 plays went for double digits. They allowed a 58.3% success rate. You could build the case that the 49ers aren’t running inside enough this season. Christian McCaffrey had two 11-yard runs on inside zone last week. McCaffrey has 24 inside zone carries this year and averages 5.04 yards per carry, with a 62.5% success rate. Add in the different motions and window dressing, and it’s tough to see the defense that allowed the best rushing attack (Tampa Bay) its face this season to run for 241 yards slow down the 49ers. Trent Williams injured his shoulder in practice and is questionable. Veteran Vederian Lowe would take Williams’ place if he cannot suit up. As big a loss as that would be for the 49ers, the Cowboys are 29th in stuff rate. They do not get stops on the ground. Their linebackers get caught up in the wash, creating massive rushing lanes. Where can Brock Purdy attack the Cowboys? The Cowboys allow a good amount of chunk plays through the air. They’re 27th in EPA per pass. They’re also 25th in passing success rate. Watching Daniel Jones forgo intermediate passes last week for underneath throws was maddening. Receivers were open. They just weren’t targeted. How has Dallas held up against elite passing offenses? C.J. Stroud threw for 347 yards. Nico Collins and Jaylin Noel each had over 85 receiving yards. Jordan Love threw for 276 yards. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson combined for nine catches and 168 yards. No Mike Evans again for the 49ers, but this should not be a defense where the Niners need their No. 1 target. The Cowboys don’t create negative plays. What Purdy will see this week compared to next is the polar opposite—the Cowboys blitz 20.2% of the time, the second-lowest mark in the league. In theory, Purdy should have plenty of time to scan the field and pick Dallas apart. It’s a Vic Fangio-adjacent defense, so the Cowboys will do all they can to take away the middle of the field and funnel targets to lower-percentage areas, like outside the numbers. Jordan Watkins has ten targets in the previous two games. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. looks set to return from injury and will look to slow down Watkins hot streak. The rookie will be on the radar Rookie Caleb Downs is the player the Niners could find success against. He’s primarily played nickel. Against the Texans, Packers, and Cardinals, Downs allowed all 9 of his targets to be completed for 147 yards. Heading into Week 9, Downs had allowed a 90.5% completion percentage, which was the third-highest among slot cornerbacks this season. He has one pass breakup. Dallas tried to align him closer to the line of scrimmage, almost like a pseudo-linebacker in coverage against Arizona. He played linebacker 32.1% of the time against the Cardinals. But now he’s facing an offense that thrives over the middle. Downs has nowhere to hide against the Niners. Old friend Kendrick Bourne caught a slant on Downs, broke a tackle, and gained a bunch of yards en route to a 29-yard gain. Downs was no match for Trey McBride on a 3rd-and-6 target— hello, George Kittle. Downs is not a big player. He’s 5’11”, 206 pounds, but has a 10th percentile arm length. That shows up in contested situations when he can’t make plays on the ball. Savion Williams from the Packers got Downs a couple of times on in-breaking routes. Watson and Golden each had a double-digit reception against Watkins on an out route on third down. He would’ve allowed two first-down receptions on third down last week to the Colts, but his brother dropped the ball both times. You better believe the rookie will be on the 49ers’ radar. Whether it’s the No. 1, 2, or slot receiver, the Cowboys are bottom-three in yards after the catch allowed per reception. The No. 2 third-down offense meets the 32nd third-down defense. The No. 1 red zone offense meets the No. 25 red zone defense. Dallas also has six more defensive penalties than the 31st-placed team. On paper, the only thing stopping the 49ers from scoring in this game is the 49ers. Outside of Quinnen Williams, this defense has zero redeeming qualities. Will the Cowboys fumble the game away like the Raiders? The 49ers forced five turnovers, masking the Raiders’ six potential scoring drives. Luck plays a role in every turnover. To date, the Cowboys are 22nd in turnover EPA lost per game on offense. They make mistakes. Look no further than last week when Dak Prescott fumbled on third down, or CeeDee Lamb fumbled going into score. Fred Warner and the Niners defense have a penchant for the peanut punch. They’re sixth this year at forcing fumbles, thanks in large part to the soon-to-be Defensive Player of the Year. Most potent offense the 49ers have faced to date Starting cornerbacks Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir practiced Friday for the first time. Nate Hobbs practiced in full and could make his debut, especially with Upton Stout banged up. It’ll be all hands on deck to slow down the most potent offense on the schedule yet. Raheem Morris has been a godsend for this organization. He’s developed a scheme that is third at limiting explosive plays and fifth in yards per attempt. The biggest surprise is the 49ers being first in EPA per rush this season. Warner plays a significant role in limited targets over the middle. Teams are terrified to throw the ball between the numbers at 5 and 15 yards. The 49ers have allowed 31 yards per game, the best in the NFL. Their explosive play rate of 5% is also the league-leading rate. That’s better than 9% of the league average. But this will be the first team in the top 8 in EPA per pass that the defense has faced. No Jake Ferguson is a big blow; Lamb, George Pickens, and Ryan Flournoy provide plenty of firepower. Another area the 49ers have been fantastic at is taking away throws to the slot. The Niners allow slot receivers a 51% target share, good for second-lowest in the league. All the post-snap spinning they do at safety, paired with that Warner guy lurking, forces the quarterback to throw outside the numbers. It’s worked to date, but there haven’t been a Lamb and Pickens on the outside, either. The best receiver the 49ers faced this season, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, had 102 yards on five catches. Brock Bowers had 111 receiving yards last week. Trey McBride had 75 yards back in September. Those are the three players the team’s game plan is built around, and the Niners failed to stop any of them. It’d be a breath of fresh air to see the Niners’ cornerbacks be competitive in this spot. One thing they have going for them is the game script. The Cowboys may not want to run the ball against San Francisco, even if it’s great on great. Dallas is fifth in rushing success rate. But you won’t run the ball if you’re constantly trailing on the scoreboard. Prescott, like Kirk Cousins, does not take sacks. This season, the 49ers lead the league in sack percentage on offense at 3%. The Raiders are right behind them at 3.2%. Dallas ranks fifth at 3.8%. Dallas is also eighth in pressure rate allowed. Things change when the run threat no longer exists. The Niners’ defensive line feasts on obvious passing downs. Osa Odighizuwa gets a shot at redemption from the team that traded him. Keion White and Romello Height get to pin their ears back, while veterans DeForest Buckner and Nick Bosa get their second game together. When you filter to players with at least 350 passing snaps, the Cowboys tackles rank third and fourth in the highest blown-block rate in the NFL at 5.3% and 5.2%, with a combined eight sacks. For reference, Colton McKivitz has a blown-block rate of 2.3%, and Trent Williams is at 2%. The 49ers were built to play with a lead and harass one-dimensional offenses. Dallas will score. They’ll probably score a lot. But Prescott will be under pressure to keep pace with Purdy. San Francisco isn’t the only team stepping up in class. The Cowboys scored 20 points against the Giants in Week 1, but failed to surpass 17 points against the two other playoff defenses they faced this season. It might be premature to assume that’ll change against a defense ranked sixth in the NFL in points allowed per game. The Cowboys can hurt you on third down (5th) and in the red zone (3rd). The only area outside of sacks where the Niners are below league average is on third downs. One turnover. One punt. One mishap. That’s all it’s taken so far this season, and that’ll likely continue for the 49ers on the road against a team with high expectations coming into the year, but that has failed to live up to the talent. (Something we never say about the Cowboys.) 49ers 38, Cowboys 30.

stories.title: Cowboys aggressiveness on offense must be turned up vs. 49ers
stories.summary: What do the upset-minded Cowboys need to do at home to beat the 49ers?
stories.detailText: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images After two straight weeks of early window kickoffs in which the Dallas Cowboys had to fight, claw, scratch, and get knocked down to go 1-1 against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, they play in the Sunday late afternoon window against the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are off a win, which puts the Cowboys right back in a position they’ve been time and time again and failed in nearly every time, trying to win consecutive games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys can’t afford to spin their wheels much longer if they want to make this season mean something though. This 49ers matchup is exactly that opportunity for the Cowboys, so let’s get to how they can pull off the upset. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the San Francisco 49ers if… …they win on 1st down on both offense and defense. Think for a second about how many NFL offenses are truly earning the label of “elite”, “scary”, or “explosive” right now, then without looking at any other metrics or analytics consider the top four tiers in the first downs per play category. They are the Bills, 49ers, Lions, and Bengals tied for first, the Cowboys in second, and the Jaguars and Rams in third just ahead of the Patriots and Chiefs. Also among these teams, the 49ers, Lions, and Bills are in the top five for fewest third downs faced per game. The Patriots, Chiefs, Jags, and Bengals are all virtually tied with the Bills to round out the top nine. Then there are the 14th ranked Cowboys, much closer to teams like the Steelers, Texans, and Browns – none of which have the QB situation Dallas does that should be keeping them out of this not-so-great company. This is a main culprit why they feel like outliers on the elite, scary, or explosive list while the other offenses are much more deserving. For even more evidence that the Cowboys offense is all about Dak right now, and that Prescott should be getting way more help than he is from all directions, there’s the fact two of the three touchdown drives last week at the Colts came in two minute situations before halftime and at the end of the game. The Cowboys need much more than just Prescott to be at their absolute best against the 49ers, but fairly or not will also need #4 to be among the players that elevates their game this week as well. The best path towards doing so is much more early down aggressiveness and the Cowboys embracing what they do best by throwing the ball to CeeDee Lamb, and hopefully George Pickens, not just on third down, but all the time. Without Jake Ferguson for this game, one of the things the Cowboys are going to have an incredibly difficult time doing is persuading the 49ers defense out of loading the box. They don’t have the middle of the field threat to get behind these stacked looks, especially considering the freakish coverage ability to all parts of the field from Fred Warner. Dallas will still need to find it’s times to run the ball and doing so well on early downs would also be huge, but staying in spread looks and letting Prescott make the right decision should be their bread and butter. The 49ers use motion on 71.5% of their offensive plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL. The Cowboys have allowed +0.11 EPA per play against motion, LAST in the NFL. @DLLS_Cowboys pic.twitter.com/Gq8Gr9vUrg — John Andersen (@AndersenJA) November 11, 2026 This could also allow them to use some tempo to their advantage, getting to the line quickly to give them time to use motions, something the 49ers offense is going to do a ton of to the Cowboys defense, and Cowboys offense would be wise to try to give it back. On defense, the Cowboys need to do everything they can to limit the vast amount of plays 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan can get to at all times. If Christian McCaffrey is breaking tackles and getting considerable gains on first downs all game, the 49ers are simply too talented and well-coached to be stopped. They will toy with Christian Parker’s defense when ahead of the chains with short, intermediate, and deep layered passes. There’s also the element of Brock Purdy’s effectiveness scrambling outside of the pocket, another area Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark will have to step up in pushing the pocket and keeping contain. A complete game in both run and pass defense from the Cowboys front will give them a chance to replicate what the Atlanta Falcons did to the 49ers as the only team to beat them this season. How often QBs have had perfectly blocked plays and their EPA on those plays pic.twitter.com/Erv2iR2BIO — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) November 11, 2026 The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the San Francisco 49ers if… …they are horribly outcoached. Even though the disparity in records is obvious in this game between the 7-1 49ers and 4-5 Cowboys, if the game was going to solely be decided by the players on the field, I think many fans on both sides would be expecting a much closer game than they currently are. The biggest gripe from Cowboys fans when it comes to things they’re not looking forward to the most about this toughest game of the season to date is how likely it feels the 49ers coaching staff will run laps around the Cowboys staff, and separate even more on the scoreboard as a result of it. Play Caller Tendencies 🎮 The NFC North is the only division where every offensive play caller has a positive rating. The AFC North, AFC East, and NFC West are close behind, each with at least three play callers in positive territory. pic.twitter.com/kmd5AduJDw — Steven Patton (@PattonAnalytics) November 11, 2026 This chart shows that Schottenheimer is lacking creativity in his offensive formations/plays, while Shanahan is uplifting the 49ers with his usual masterclass at taking a roster hammered by injuries and still finding a way to win. The Cowboys have already lost to four of the coaches that presently rank above Schottenheimer on this chart, play the 49ers this Sunday, then still have to play the Jaguars and Seahawks in December. The only win for Schotty against a coach above him on this list is the one directly above him by the smallest of margins, Nick Caley with the Texans. The Cowboys are finding themselves outcoached all too often right now. The Cowboys have the talent to compete with this 49ers team, and they have everything left to play for in the NFC East. If they come out and continue to have communication issues on both sides of the ball, call plays like they’re playing to not lose instead of playing to win, and shoot themselves in the foot with egregious penalties, it will be all most fans need to see that this season is doomed to look like year one under Schottenheimer and fall short of the playoffs again. A Cowboys head coach that’s had the chance to work with a healthy Dak Prescott has never had as little success as Schottenheimer is now, and Prescott has not beaten the 49ers since being with the coach that drafted him Jason Garrett in 2017. The chance for this QB-HC duo to have a real signature moment is right there for the taking in week ten if the Cowboys play their best game of the season, a challenge the Dallas coaching staff needs to rise to instead of wilting under the pressure of.

stories.title: On Kirk Cousins (and Packers Week, Too!)
stories.summary: Never boring, this team of ours.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - SEPTEMBER 13: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings passes the ball in the second quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2020 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins is once again the quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings. Welcome to the most exciting, if anxiety-riddled, stretch of Vikings football in memory. The next few months will be unlike any other. General manager Nolan Teasley did what he had to do. A 3rd-round pick was a small price to pay to avoid the iceberg. After an embarrassing, mind-boggling, inept offensive showing in front of the entire nation on Monday Night Football that threatened a full-on locker room mutiny and the season’s implosion, the ship has now been steered into calmer waters. Whether it will be there when the calendar turns to January is still very much up in the air. The only situations even remotely comparable were Sam Bradford’s arrival days before the 2016 season and Randy Moss’ return in 2010. While the former started well, defeating the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, it ultimately petered out. The latter didn’t even get that far. Let’s hope for better luck this time around. NARRATIVES, NARRATIVES EVERYWHERE! Super Bowl Dreams Are Back On. Through nine games as the Raiders’ starter, with offensive weapons no one would confuse with the 1999 Rams, Kirk Cousins was on pace for more TD passes (38) than he had with the Vikings (2021 and 2022) after the NFL moved to a 17-game regular season. He would just fall short of the passing yardage he had in 2022 (4,547). In an earlier article, I noted that a torn Achilles in a quarterback’s plant leg is the worst non-throwing-arm injury you can sustain. Recovery is challenging and often takes more than one season before you start to look like yourself again. I think that may explain much of what’s going on with Daniel Jones in Indy right now. Given his performance this year, there is a persuasive argument that the nature of the injury, not necessarily age, may explain the inconsistency Cousins experienced during his stint with the Atlanta Falcons. Would he have played better if he were 25? Probably. But his play for the Raiders has been a pleasant surprise that no one envisioned before the season: 2nd in passing TDs, 5th in yards, 9th in EPA per dropback, etc. All Cousins needs to do is be good. That’s it. The Raiders are 8th in points per game (26.4). We won’t even need that 95% of the time. We’d be 8-0 right now. The reason the Silver and Black are 4-5 is that their defense is last in points allowed (29.8) and yards allowed (385.4). They’re basically the 2020-21 Vikings. Under Brian Flores, we’re 1st and 2nd in those categories, respectively. The NFC is wide open right now. No one is convincing me that there is a team we can’t beat, with Cousins back throwing to Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson again, and Flores’ defense as the ultimate insurance policy. Cousins, Storybook Ending? Hollywood’s most gifted screenwriters couldn’t come up with a better scenario. Cousins returns to the Vikings to save the season, and his first game is at Lambeau Field – the very place his Vikings tenure ended the first time around. All under the larger theme of redemption, given how those highly debated years ended after the 2023 season. Can’t make it up: Vikings play “Higher” by Creed at Kirk Cousins’ first practice back with them. pic.twitter.com/NYLOld9d64 — Kevin Seifert (@SeifertESPN) November 12, 2026 Cousins realizes the feel-good, storybook ending is within reach. Reports say the Raiders left the trade decision in his hands. He knows. This is his last, best chance. A Kirk Cousins with a Super Bowl ring would not only have a legitimate Hall of Fame resume (the numbers will be there), but he’d also have a statue outside U.S. Stadium to immortalize his role in ending the long-suffering anguish of a tortured fan base. Patience is a virtue. I’d urge people not to expect Cousins to come in seamlessly and pick up where he left off in 2023. It may take a game or two to get back into a rhythm with the offense and receivers, regardless of previous experience. That certainly doesn’t mean we won’t win on Sunday. We’ve already beaten the Packers and have won games this season with an offense that made us long for the days of the Wishbone or Single-Wing. This is about ensuring the offense is hitting its stride heading into December and (hopefully) a memorable playoff run. KOC Gets a Mulligan (For Now). Cousins’ return effectively gives KOC a new lease on life after repeatedly stepping on rakes with disastrous quarterback decisions that necessitated the trade. He may have gotten away with the “don’t look at me!” routine in drafting J.J. McCarthy and letting Sam Darnold walk, but the 2026 quarterback room mess is on him. You can only play that hand so many times. Kwesi Adofo-Mensah took the blame for the earlier missteps and lost his job. Nolan Teasley can justifiably plead ignorance for being late to the game, and no one believes he traded McCarthy without KOC’s approval (or encouragement). Regardless of how this season ends, the Vikings will again begin the offseason back at the drawing board at the most important position on the field. The best-case scenario is that Cousins thrives and reworks his deal to replay the role he played with the Raiders this season if the Vikings try yet again to hit on the QBOTF in the draft. Or maybe they can swing a risky trade for Justin Herbert and effectively blow up their cap as several key in-house free agents loom. Does a Daniel Jones trade happen? Do people think Geno Smith or Mac Jones could be the answer? The bill for the Murray-McCarthy mess will eventually come due. Let’s hope KOC still has the currency to pay it without breaking a sweat. I’ve said before that the best-case scenario and the Vikings often go together like hot fudge and sushi. But we’re due for a break after botching the quarterback situation as badly as possible, only to go back to where we started. Right? Right? Kirk Cousins isn’t coming back in another three years to save us again. Well, we are the Vikings, so you never know. That wouldn’t even crack the Top 20 for the weirdest things to happen to this franchise. OH YEAH, THE PACKERS… With Vikings fans and the Minnesota district manager at Kohl’s basking in the excitement of the Cousins trade and renewed hopes for a Super Bowl run, there is a game to play against the stupid Green Bay Packers. As much as it pains me to say it, the Packers come into this one on a roll. They thoroughly destroyed the New England Patriots on the road last week and have won five of their last six. Vikings on Offense All eyes will be on Kirk Cousins and the Vikings offense. The good news is that as long as Cousins doesn’t miss the team bus, it’ll immediately be an improvement over what we’ve seen recently. Like last season without Micah Parsons, the Packers’ defense is good, if not quite elite. He’s close to returning but won’t play in this one. They’re 11th in both points and total yards allowed, but better (Top 5) in yards per play and defensive DVOA. Pass defense is their strength, as they’re in the Top 10 in both pass EPA allowed and passer rating allowed. The Packers have also feasted on interceptions and are 2nd in the NFL. Their run defense looks to be middle of the pack across most traditional and advanced metrics. Hopefully this can be exploited early to get Cousins comfortable and open up the play-action pass game he excelled at under KOC the first time around. I’m genuinely curious how much of the playbook will be open to Cousins with such a short prep, regardless of familiarity. KOC may have commented on this, but if he did, I missed it. As I noted above, however, it may be too much to expect him to just drop in and play as if he never left. Give it some time. What matters is how this offense looks heading into December. Vikings on Defense Quarterback Jordan Love has the offense leading the NFL in passing yards per game. This has translated into strong showings for the dangerous receiving trio of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft. Those three had a field day against us in Week 1, but that was mostly in the first half, before we woke up and realized the season had started. This version will not be rusty and will surely have resolved the communication and coverage issues that plagued the unit two months ago. The problem for the Cheeseheads is that their running game is abysmal, ranking 32nd, and they don’t have an injured Josh Jacobs to lean on. I’d think this works in the Vikings’ favor, as it will force the Packers’ offense to play the game on our terms. If the pass vs. run dynamic were flipped, or even more balanced, that would concern me a bit more. That said, Love and the Packers’ aerial attack are incredibly dangerous, stellar Vikings pass defense or not. We’d better be ready. Prediction There are a lot of things that worry me about this game for the Vikings: Cousins’ comfort level, not helped by an offensive line playing particularly well, likely missing Blake Cashman, who is having an All-Pro season, and the Packers’ passing offense clicking on all cylinders. Counterpoints: 1. Comfortable or not, Cousins can hit an open receiver. 2. Brian Flores. I’m not letting this high wear off. No way, no how. The running game shows some life now that opposing defenses have to worry about the passing game. This, in turn, opens up some much-needed (and desperately missed) Cousins-to-Jefferson/Addison/Hockenson (if he plays) highlights. Just enough to get the job done on Sunday, with improvements to come. Let’s party like it’s 2022 (on offense). Minnesota Vikings: 23 Green Bay Packers: 21

stories.title: 49ers OT Williams, LB Greenlaw questionable, WR Evans out vs. Cowboys
stories.summary: The 49ers are listing left tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, while receiver Mike Evans has been ruled out.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers had two important additions to their injury report this week with left tackle Trent Williams (shoulder) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (knee) now listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys . According to coach Kyle Shanahan, Williams and Greenlaw suffered their injuries in Thursday's practice, with both players listed as limited for that day because of it. Greenlaw was again limited Friday, while Williams did not practice. "Anytime you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn't make you totally at ease," Shanahan said of Williams. "Sunday comes fast, but hopefully that's enough time for him to be all right." If Williams is unable to play, the Niners will turn to swing tackle Vederian Lowe to step into the lineup. And if Greenlaw can't play, rookie Jaden Dugger will move into the weakside linebacker spot, according to Shanahan. "Hopefully we'll have Dre on Sunday, but if we don't, next man up, and our next man's proven himself so far," Shanahan said. Elsewhere on the injury report, wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) will miss his third straight game. He's the only Niner officially ruled out against the Cowboys as he continues to work his way through the tendinitis that flared up in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders . Shanahan offered a bit more clarity Friday afternoon on when Evans could return, saying there's "a chance" for next week against the Minnesota Vikings but adding that he's "not sure yet." "It's been going well," Shanahan said. "I'm sure if this was the last game or something, he'd be able to go out there. But we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again, but it's going in the right direction." In addition to Williams and Greenlaw, all three of San Francisco's top cornerbacks -- Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) -- are questionable against the Cowboys. So, too, are defensive tackle C.J. West (knee) and defensive back Nate Hobbs (adductor), both of whom are working their way back from injured reserve and could be activated Saturday. Meanwhile, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who has been out with a hamstring injury since Week 5, practiced all week and is cleared to return against the Cowboys. "He had a good week, healthy," Shanahan said. "First week back, so he's still getting back into it, but [he] took care of himself real well while he was injured and had a good week."

stories.title: Vikings to start reacquired QB Kirk Cousins vs. Packers
stories.summary: Coach Kevin O'Connell called Kirk Cousins' ability to get reacquainted with the Vikings' offense "impressive."
stories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- Although there wasn't much question about it, Minnesota Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed Friday that quarterback Kirk Cousins will start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers , five days after the Vikings reacquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline. "I can't give him enough credit for coming in here and how he's gone about the week," O'Connell said, "both him and the coaching staff, getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can. It's been really impressive what he's been able to do, and just the command and getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody has been very, very impressed with." In the immediate aftermath of the trade, O'Connell had stopped short of naming Cousins his starter for Sunday, saying he wanted to make sure the veteran felt comfortable with the quick turnaround. The two spent much of Wednesday morning together, working through a playbook that Cousins first learned when the Vikings hired O'Connell in 2022. Since departing Minnesota after the 2023 season, Cousins has played for both the Raiders and the Atlanta Falcons . He had only two practices this week with the Vikings, on Thursday and Friday, but O'Connell saw no red flags. "It's something we've always known about him," O'Connell said, "but the way he threw the football this week was just a really cool thing to see." Cousins, however, won't have his full complement of pass catchers to work with Sunday. Tight end T.J. Hockenson won't play because of wrist and chest injuries suffered in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Wide receiver Jordan Addison , meanwhile, was added to the injury report Friday because of a thumb injury suffered in practice. The Vikings listed him as questionable. stories.title: Buffalo Bills safety Amani Hooker will make his debut Week 10 vs. NY Jets
stories.summary: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady says safety Amani Hooker is set to make his debut against the New York Jets Week 10
stories.detailText: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Amani Hooker #37 of the Tennessee Titans reacts after making an interception during an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took all of three practices for Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady to decide that Amani Hooker, the team’s new addition at safety, will play in Week 10 against the New York Jets. In meeting with members of the media, Brady revealed that Hooker “definitely is gonna play, and excited to see whatever that role kind of looks like.” The Bills and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane knew the time was right to take advantage of the looming trade deadline. In doing so, Buffalo has brought in someone they immediately identified as a starter for defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s system. Brady, ever the master press chess player, was careful not to reveal too much about their plans for Hooker. He did say that play time is yet to be determined, noting that “from a comfort level, we don’t want to put him out there and do anything that is not fair to him and the team.” Brady and the team’s defensive coaches have been impressed with Hooker’s ability to quickly assimilate within the team’s defense, including the ability to “communicate in our language.” Hooker’s arrival means that once again veteran safety Damar Hamlin is likely to take a step back into a reserve role. Despite that, Hamlin has embraced his new teammate, helping him get comfortable with his new role in Buffalo. Brady was asked about Hamlin and he emphatically stated that “Damar Hamlin has an incredibly important role on this football team, and he’s gonna play a big part on this football team in a lot of different areas.”He did acknowledge that Hooker’s arrival might prove frustrating for Hamlin, who seemed to play well the last two games, and spoke about the situation at length, saying: “Look, regardless of (if) someone says it or not, anytime you have an opportunity to be a starter and then you trade for somebody else, it can be a natural tendency to kind of maybe get frustrated. Right? But I believe Damar, and the safeties, and the team — we have a lot of guys on this team that can put pride aside and say ‘hey whatever we gotta do to win a football game’… …that’s what Damar Hamlin’s all about and that’s what he’s always been about. He just wants opportunities to compete, and he’s out there competing. And if it helps the Buffalo Bills, that’s what he’s about. So, that’s why we love him and that’s why — the trade was not an indication of Damar Hamlin, and more so just an opportunity for us to improve our football team.” Though Hooker will, in fact, make his Bills debut in Week 10, it’s possible we still see Hamlin in action on defense depending on the situation. He may also reclaim a significant role on special teams, where the last two games Hamlin played zero snaps with the special teams units.

Mahomes then connected with newly acquired Josh Downs for a 12-yard gain and another first down. The reception moved the Chiefs to the Falcons’ 25-yard line. Two plays later, Xavier Watts intercepted Mahomes on a high throw intended for Rashee Rice running a crossing route. stories.title: Vikings name Week 10 starter vs Packers after Kirk Cousins trade
stories.summary: The Minnesota Vikings plan to have quarterback Kirk Cousins make his debut in Week 10. Is he the starter against the Packers?
stories.detailText: The Minnesota Vikings finally made the announcement that many have been expecting for several days. Quarterback Kirk Cousins will start against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced on Friday, Nov. 13. The intra-divisional game will mark the start of Cousins' second stint in Minnesota, three years after his last game for the Vikings . "Kirk Cousins will start the football game. Cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he's gone about the week. Both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can," O'Connell said. "It's been really impressive, what he's been able to do ... just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed by. Excited to start Kirk in the game, see him play on Sunday." .oembed-frame {width:100%;height:100%;margin:0;border:0;} Kevin O'Connell announces Kirk Cousins will start Sunday in Green Bay. https://t.co/0ERsgfpEuX — Bring Me The Sports (@BMTNSports) November 13, 2026 KIRK COUSINS: Veteran QB kept mum about his chance to start Week 10 Coincidentally, the upcoming Nov. 15 clash will be Cousins' second straight matchup against the Packers as the Vikings' starting quarterback. The last game the 38-year-old played for Minnesota, in 2023, was also at Lambeau Field. Cousins' first stint with the Vikings ended unceremoniously – trainers had to cart him off of the field after he tore his Achilles during a game his team went on to win. In the offseason that followed, the Vikings allowed him to walk in free agency, and he went on to sign a four-year, $180 million contract with the Atlanta Falcons . Cousins said in his (re-)introductory press conference with the Vikings on Nov. 11 that he expects the Week 10 game to be meaningful. It's both his first game back with Minnesota but also his return to Lambeau Field for the first time since the 2023 injury. "It means a lot to play at Lambeau Field, no matter what the circumstances," Cousins said. "Knowing that that was where I was carted off, and I had thoughts of, 'Is this my last game? Is this my last game as a Viking?' To be back out there, wearing the purple and gold. It has meaning, but you have to go make it mean something with the way you play." In nine starts with the Las Vegas Raiders this season, Cousins has a 4-5 record. He was 202-of-315 passing for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. His 97.1 passer rating so far this season is his highest since his previous stint with Minnesota. The Vikings are hoping the addition of Cousins will help kick-start an offensive resurgence. The team has lost two straight following a 6-0 start, and it sits in third place in a tightly contested NFC North. While the defense has been a strong point – the 14.5 points per game the unit has allowed so far is the fewest in the league – the offense has struggled. Minnesota's 18.3 points scored per game are sixth-fewest in the NFL. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Vikings name Week 10 starter vs Packers after Kirk Cousins trade

stories.title: NFL outlines steps in Jalen Hurts investigation in letter to senator
stories.summary: The NFL provided some additional details about the investigation into how Jalen Hurts' blood clots were handled in response to an inquiry from a U.S. senator.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- Independent medical experts will examine the circumstances around Jalen Hurts ' blood clots and share their findings with the NFL and NFL Players Association as part of the forthcoming joint review, according to a league executive. The NFL provided some additional details about the review as well as its protocols for tracking blood clots in response to an inquiry from U.S. Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware. "As outlined by the league and NFLPA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties," executive vice president of communications, public affairs and health policy Jeff Miller said in a statement released by Blunt Rochester's office Friday. "The League and Players Association also have several medical committees that review and monitor player injury data closely. For at least the past decade, the NFL has tracked clotting disorders among players every season through a subcommittee of its General Medical Committee, and this information is shared with the NFLPA. Following the ongoing joint review, the League and NFLPA will consider appropriate next steps, including whether this case points to a need for additional league-wide guidance." The joint review into Hurts' situation has not officially begun as the NFL and NFLPA work to hammer out its parameters. Hurts, 28, is expected to sit out the rest of the 2026 season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs in October. He was originally diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London before the Philadelphia Eagles ' Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars . He played in the game, flew home with the team and practiced in full the following Wednesday before a follow-up ultrasound that evening showed the blood clot had moved. Hurts was placed on injured reserve Oct. 17. Two days later, his agent, Nicole Lynn, and the team released a joint statement about Hurts, saying, "After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations." His treatment involves anticoagulation or "blood thinners," which prevents him from participating in any contact activities, including football. The NFLPA has not invoked Article 39 of the CBA, which allows the union to launch a formal investigation into the health, safety or medical care provided by club-affiliated personnel, but as the statement shows, some of its guidelines will be used during this process. Under the CBA, the neutral physicians must issue a written report within 60 days of their selection, and their recommendations to address and correct any issues need to be acted upon by both parties. Blunt Rochester penned a letter to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in October seeking answers on the circumstances surrounding Hurts and clarity on the league's blood clot protocols. In a statement Friday, Blunt Rochester expressed gratitude to the NFL for providing an update while encouraging the league to use its platform to further education around blood clots. "We welcome the opportunity to provide additional information, and find ways to support your efforts around raising awareness and improving outcomes related to blood clot disorders," Miller wrote.

stories.title: Vikings down key pieces for Week 10 matchup with Packers

stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings is tackled by Zaire Franklin #44 of the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter of the game on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images If the Minnesota Vikings want to repeat their Week 1 win over the Packers, they’re going to have to do it shorthanded. They’ve already ruled out five players for Sunday’s game, including tight end T.J. Hockenson and linebacker Blake Cashman. Hockenson hasn’t practiced yet this week with a combination of wrist and chest injuries. His absence will deprive the Vikings — and newly acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins — of one of their most productive receivers. Hockenson ranks first on the team with 35 catches and is second in yards with 328. Though he averages just 9.4 yards per catch, he’d have been a reliable and steady help for Cousins as he settles back into his familiar Minnesota environs. Cashman, meanwhile, has been in the concussion protocol all week. He leads the Vikings with 76 total tackles and is also a key part of the Vikings’ pressure scheme; his 4.5 sacks are the second most on the team, while his eight tackles for loss are tied for the team lead. The Vikings also ruled out defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, wide receiver Jauan Jennings, and quarterback Kyler Murray. Though Murray’s absence is basically immaterial at this point, Ingram-Dawkins and Jennings are noteworthy. Ingram-Dawkins was a significant part of the Vikings’ defensive line rotation, playing just a hair under 58% of the Vikings’ defensive snaps this year. Jennings was more of a supporting player for the wide receiver-rich Vikings. Behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, Jennings had only logged six catches in six games. But Addison also finds himself questionable for Sunday, putting the Vikings in a bit of a wide receiver bind with Jennings already ruled out. (And not for nothing, Jennings had five catches for 61 yards against the Packers in the 2023 playoffs as a member of the San Francisco 49ers. I just assume that any random role player who ever had a good game against the Packers has their number forever. It seems like it just works out that way.) In any case, the Vikings won’t be dealing from a full deck when they visit the Packers on Sunday. That’s good news as the Packers try to continue their climb toward the top of the NFC North, especially since the Packers’ injury report is anything but short as well .

Shanahan wouldn’t give a concrete answer about the concern level surrounding Williams. “Any time you hurt your shoulder on a Thursday, it doesn’t make you totally at ease. Sunday comes fast. But hopefully, that’s enough time for him to be all right.” Shanahan said Evans’ recovery is “going well.” He added, “I’m sure if it was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. But we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals, so it doesn’t act up again. Keenan Allen “had a good week” of practice and “will have a role” Sunday against the Cowboys. How big of a role that is remains to be seen. Deebo Samuel is “healthy.” Shanahan said he’s a full go. The 49ers worked out a right-footed punter, but Shanahan said that was more for Cowing, the punt returner. “Just the spin of the ball. Always seeing it turn one way. It’s the same with punts. Catching punts is one of the hardest things in sports. You can’t get enough work of it.” Corliss Waitman, the Niners punter, is left-footed. stories.title: Packers must corral Vikings return man Myles Price
stories.summary: Vikings return ace Myles Price might be a difference maker on Sunday.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings’ defense is incredible. Their offense should be more capable with a new quarterback under center. But their special teams also present a very interesting challenge for the Packers. Under the guidance of new coordinator Cam Achord, the Packers’ special teams have been — with some exceptions — generally pretty solid. Pre-injury, Skyy Moore bolstered the Packers’ return game, but the Packers’ special teams have really shined in coverage. As of this week, the Packers’ have allowed the fourth-lowest average per return on punt returns and the 10th lowest figure on special teams. (This, incidentally, aligns with the special teams stuff the Packers have historically cared about the most and done the best, but it’s still good to see them doing a good job there.) But as good as the Packers are in punt and kick coverage, the Vikings are even better at punt and kick returns. Minnesota currently ranks first in punt return average (17.5 yards per return) and second in kickoff return average (29.9 per return). It’s true the Vikings have logged a very long punt return (86 yards) and a pretty long kickoff return (68 yards), but even if you removed those long returns, the Vikings’ averages would only drop them to the fifth- and third-best spots in the league on punt and kickoff return, respectively. And it’s all thanks to return man Myles Price. Undrafted out of Indiana in 2025, the 5-foot-9, 183-pound Price was a special teams only player for the Vikings last season. He averaged a respectable 9.9 yards per return on 30 punt returns and 25.9 yards per return on 60 kickoff returns, but capped out at a long of 43 yards on his punt duties and 61 yards on kickoff returns. Certainly not bad numbers, but not eye popping. That’s changed in 2026. The pocket-sized Price leads the NFL in punt return yardage, boasts the longest punt return in the league, and is the only player in the NFL to score on a punt return this season. He’s also the only player who’s returned either a punt or a kick for the Vikings this year, meaning their impressive league-wide rankings are entirely the work of their micro machine return man. Everybody knows the Packers will have their hands full with Brian Flores, and Kirk Cousins may be enough to bolster their offense to at least some level of respectability. But if the Packers don’t take care of business on special teams, the Vikings could end up tilting the balance in that phase of the game. And in what’s expected to be a close game, any little bit could make a difference. Fortunately, special teams have never been a game-altering problem for the Packers in the past, right? Right?

stories.summary: Center Hjalte Froholdt will miss his first start since joining the Cardinals in 2023.
stories.detailText: Center Hjalte Froholdt will miss his first start since joining the Cardinals in 2023. Froholdt did not clear concussion protocol, ruling him out for Sunday's game against the Rams. Froholdt had started all possible 60 games since signing as a free agent. The Cardinals will also play without offensive lineman Jon Gaines II (ankle). That means Hayden Conner will start at center. Defensive lineman Zach Carter, who has had three limited practices since coming off injured reserve with a knee injury, is also out. The Cardinals list tight end Hunter Long (knee), defensive lineman Roy Lopez (toe/ankle), cornerback Max Melton (knee/hand), defensive lineman Darius Robinson (wrist), left tackle Jayden Williams (knee) and safety Dewey Wingard (groin) as questionable. Lopez returned to practice on Friday, as did Robinson, who was a DNP on Thursday. Robinson had a wrap on his wrist. Long would have to be activated to the 53-player roster by Saturday afternoon if he is to return this week.

stories.title: Packers Injury Report: Green Bay rules out 4 vs. Vikings
stories.summary: Center Sean Rhyan is among four who won’t play for the Packers on Sunday
stories.detailText: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have officially ruled out four players on Friday: running back Josh Jacobs (finger), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee/illness-PUP), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle. Of those three players, only Jacobs played against the New England Patriots last week, and he did not finish the game. Yesterday, head coach Matt LaFleur stated that Jacobs had yet to have surgery on his fractured ring finger, but that it would be coming in the near future. The Packers used the doubtful status, which they rarely use, on linebacker Zaire Franklin, who has been out for multiple weeks with a shin fracture. He was a non-participant throughout the week’s practices. The questionable players going into Sunday’s action are: running back Chris Brooks (ankle-IR), safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), offensive lineman Travis Glover (knee), safety Xavier McKinney (foot), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle-IR), edge defender Lukas Van Ness (back) and guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps). In total, 9 of the active roster’s 53 players were given game statuses for this week’s action against the Minnesota Vikings, leaving just 44 fully healthy players on the roster. Considering that teams need 48 players to suit up for game days, that’s a bit problematic. My guess? The questionable players are more likely than not to play on Sunday, just because the Packers are going to need bodies — and their injured reserve designations are quickly evaporating . Already, Green Bay has used four of their eight allotted return designations this season — with the practice windows now open for Brooks and Moore. And that’s with Jacob Monk, Jonathan Ford and Warren Brinson having the potential to return this season — along with some potential moves, like Jacobs going on IR, coming down the line. The Packers already were able to withstand not having Rhyan, Whyle and Franklin on the roster in recent weeks, and Jacobs will likely be replaced by MarShawn Lloyd — who missed last week’s action — on the game-day roster. As long as the questionable players are ready to go, Green Bay shouldn’t need to shake things up too much. If they aren’t, though, their reinforcements are thin right now, and we’ll probably get a heads-up on who won’t be able to play by way of the team’s Saturday practice squad elevations. stories.title: Kirk Cousins will start for Vikings on Sunday
stories.summary: The Vikings acquired the quarterback in a trade with the Raiders on Tuesday.
stories.detailText: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell wouldn't commit to Kirk Cousins as the team's starter earlier this week. O'Connell made it official on Friday, though, announcing Cousins will start against the Packers. The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders at Tuesday's trade deadline, in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. He practiced with the team Thursday and Friday, but Cousins' familiarity with the offense allowed him to step right into the starting job. Cousins was with the Vikings from 2018-23, the last two years with O'Connell. The two were also together in 2017 with Washington. Kyler Murray started six games before he injured his hamstring. Carson Wentz started Monday night's loss to the Bills and had the worst game by a Vikings' starting quarterback since 2006. Murray is ruled out for Sunday's game after not practicing all week. The Vikings also ruled out linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion), tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle) and wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf). Outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy (calf), wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) and safety Josh Metellus (shoulder) are questionable.

stories.title: Eagles release wide receiver Hollywood Brown per request
stories.summary: Receiver Hollywood Brown, who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Eagles upon his request.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- Wide receiver Hollywood Brown , who has played sparingly over the first half of the season, has been released by the Philadelphia Eagles on Friday upon his request. The two sides came to terms on a noninjury settlement that will offer financial relief to Philadelphia as part of the agreement, a source told ESPN. The Eagles are comfortable moving on from Brown with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks due to soon return from injuries, and with Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon emerging as solid options. Brown, 29, signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Philadelphia this offseason. He was brought in along with Wicks, Elijah Moore and Lemon to help complement Smith following the trade of A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots . A significant role for Brown never materialized, however, even with injuries to Smith and Wicks. He appeared in four games (one start) and had five catches for 63 yards on eight targets. All five of his catches resulted in first downs. Brown acknowledged he anticipated playing more when he joined the team but said he wasn't taking anything personally. "I wouldn't have handled it well as a younger guy," Brown said in October as questions swirled about whether he'd be traded before the Nov. 10 deadline. "It's God's plan, and the more I got comfortable with that, I can't be mad about a situation because maybe that's not what God called for. "Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play," he added, "but at the end of the day, it's not my plan." Brown has played for the Eagles, Kansas City Chiefs , Arizona Cardinals and Baltimore Ravens over his eight-year career. He had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Chiefs in 2025.

stories.summary: Let’s take a look at the Panthers key roster moves and the injury report heading into this week’s matchup.
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, NC - DECEMBER 22: Carolina Panthers guard Brady Christensen (70) and Carolina Panthers guard Damien Lewis (68) during an NFL football game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Carolina Panthers on December 22, 2024 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte N.C.(Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries For once, the Panthers got some good news on the injury front heading into their Week 10 showdown against the New Orleans Saints. Offensive lineman Brady Christensen nearly returned from injury last week, but was held out to ensure he was fully ready to go. Hopefully this is the week the versatile player can help plug one of the many, many holes on the Panthers offensive line. He’s currently listed as questionable for Sunday. Speaking of the Panthers offensive line, guard Damien Lewis was a full participant in practice on both Wednesday and Friday, though he was limited on Thursday. The incumbent starter has missed the Panthers last two games. He looks good to go Sunday. The Panthers have three additional questionable players this week in outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, cornerback Will Lee, and wide receiver Xavier Legette. Carolina could definitely use all three of them, at least situationally. Both cornerback Mike Jackson and running back Jonathon Brooks are doubtful, while linebacker Bobby Okereke is out. Transactions Signed LB Claudin Cherelus to the practice squad The Panthers have brought back linebacker Claudin Cherelus to the practice squad after waiving him back in September with an injury designation. This is Cherelus’s fourth season in Carolina after beginning his NFL career with the Panthers as an undrafted free agent back in 2023. He has appeared in 35 games for the Panthers with six starts, registering 61 tackles. Released WR David Moore then signed to the practice squad Since joining the Carolina Panthers in 2024, wide receiver David Moore has been a fixture on the roster more for his veteran stability than his actual on-field productivity. This past week the Panthers waived him then re-signed him to the practice squad, just in case the wide receiver room suffers any more injuries. This year Moore has appeared in six games with one reception 27 yards. He has also returned four punts and eight kickoffs this year. Signed DT Cam Horsley to the practice squad Cam Horsley joined the Tennessee Titans last year as an undrafted rookie free agent out of Boston College. To his credit, he made the 53-man roster and appeared in one game, playing 14 defensive snaps without recording any stats. Horsley is a diamond in the rough the Panthers will look to polish to provide some additional depth along the defensive interior. Placed WR Ihmir Smith-Marsette on practice squad-injured Ihmir Smith-Marsette is a bit of a blast from the past for Panthers fans. He joined the Panthers in 2023, which was his third NFL season at the time. He saw the field, too, appearing in all 17 games that year as Carolina’s primary punt returner who also had 11 kick returns. Back in 2023 he also contributed eight receptions for 51 yards and eight carries for 74 more yards. He left Carolina for the New York Jets in 2024, then didn’t appear in any games in 2025. The Panthers added him to the practice squad back in September 2026, and now he has an injury designation.

stories.title: The Packers’ Defense Is Living on Takeaways
stories.summary: Halfaway through the season, the Packers defense already has more takeaways than last season combined.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nine games into 2026, the Green Bay Packers’ defense has 19 takeaways: 13 interceptions and 6 fumble recoveries. Last season, they had 14 in 17 games. Sunday’s 45-27 win in Foxborough made it six straight games with multiple takeaways. Green Bay took the ball away four times and turned those turnovers into 21 points. What stands out is that it isn’t coming from blitzing. Against New England, Green Bay never rushed more than four, and all three interceptions came with Drake Maye in a clean pocket. The Packers are winning after the snap, with disguise, rotation and safeties who read the quarterback. The safeties set the tone Safeties Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams have nine takeaways between them, almost half the team’s total. McKinney leads the team with five interceptions, including two-pick games against Chicago and New England. On Sunday, he picked off Maye’s first pass of the game and returned it to the New England 14. Later he read Maye’s eyes from a deep-quarter alignment and drove on a backside dig. Williams has three interceptions and a fumble recovery. His pick against the Patriots came off a Brandon Cisse deflection on a deep shot, with Williams rotating over the top while McKinney was used as a rusher. Everyone’s getting in on it Nine different defenders have a takeaway. Six of them have an interception. Isaiah McDuffie had the best all-around day in Week 9. He stepped up when Ty’Ron Hopper left with a chest injury and became the first Packer since 2000 with multiple tackles for loss, a sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in one game. His strip-and-recover of Rhamondre Stevenson in the third quarter ended any thought of a Patriots comeback. McDuffie also has two forced fumbles. Javon Bullard, Zaire Franklin, Devonte Wyatt and Anthony Campbell have one each. Doing it shorthanded Green Bay has done this without its biggest name. The defense has played all nine games without All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons. It has also lost linebackers Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin, and three defensive tackles, to injured reserve. A defense that can’t count on pressure has had to take the ball away with coverage instead. So far it has worked: the Packers are 6-3 and have won five of their last six. Takeaway rates swing a lot from year to year, and some regression should be expected. Still, a defense whose turnovers come from disguise and safety play has a sturdier base than one living on tipped balls.

teamStories.summary: QB Drew Lock will start again for Darnold. LB Uchenna Nwosu and WR Rashid Shaheed will return to the field in Las Vegas.
teamStories.detailText: RENTON, Wash. - Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock had a good week of practice as he prepares to fill in again for Sam Darnold on Sunday against the 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders (4:05 p.m. ET, CBS) -- this time despite a pair of ailments of his own. Lock was already dealing with an injury to his right elbow when he hurt his oblique last Sunday in Seattle's 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals . He was again limited in practice all week, as has been the case since the start of Week 6. "Similar cadence in workload in terms of last week," Macdonald said Friday. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape." In addition to Darnold (quad, rib) and left guard Quenton Nelson (knee) -- whom Macdonald had ruled out earlier in the week -- the Seahawks will be without defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) and left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) again Sunday. They'll get outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and wide receiver/kick returner Rashid Shaheed (knee) back against the Raiders after each missed the past two games. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed will play Sunday after missing two days this week to tend to a personal matter. Lock said Thursday that he was feeling good, and that his oblique injury wasn't impacting his throwing all that much. It's on his right side, which Lock said is "way better" for a right-handed quatrerback than a left oblique injury, which caused him to miss two weeks during the preseason when he was with the New York Giants in 2024. "I feel like we did a great job handling the week last week, and here we are, we've just got a little something added to it, and I think we're doing the same," Lock said. "We're doing a great job getting ready." Macdonald volunteered that No. 3 quarterback Jalen Milroe "has done a tremendous job" while taking reps with the Seahawks' No. 1 offense as the team continues to manage Lock's workload in practice. Sunday's game will mark Lock's third start this season and the fourth time he's stepped in for Darnold, who hurt his glute on the fifth play of the opener, then suffered a cracked rib and a quad injury in Week 8. Macdonald has said Darnold might be able to return for the Seahawks' game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, following their bye. "I see Sam progressing with his rehab," Macdonald said. "The guys are saying he's doing a great job and he's progressing. We'll take it a day and a week at a time." Williams will miss his second straight game due to a stinger. He took part in pre-practice warmups on Wednesday and Thursday but was listed as a non-participant all week. "It's more of a contact thing," Macdonald said. "So he's done a good job of staying in shape and staying fresh. He's in the meetings. He's doing all the Leo things. He's just not playing right now." Josh Jones will make a third consecutive start at left tackle for Cross, who also did not practice this week. Macdonald said Cross should be ready for the 49ers game on Nov. 29.

teamStories.title: Las Vegas Raiders-Seattle Seahawks FEED Topic: Monitoring Fernando Mendoza’s 1st start
teamStories.summary: The day we’ve been waiting for is finally here, but it couldn’t have come against a much tougher defense.
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images While Kirk Cousins exceeded expectations as the Las Vegas Raiders’ starting quarterback, getting the team to a 4-5 record and in the playoff mix at the halfway point of the season, Week 10 against the Seattle Seahawks will be the official start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas . John Spytek, Klint Kubiak and the Raiders’ coaching staff determined that the rookie is ready for action, trading Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a third-round pick and naming Mendoza the starter. That creates plenty of excitement throughout the organization and fanbase. However, the No. 1 pick’s first start couldn’t have come against a much tougher opponent. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald has a reputation as a “defensive mastermind”, running a scheme that has a lot of moving parts and can create confusion for opposing quarterbacks, both from a pressure and coverage standpoint. For example, Seattle’s defense ranks first in yards per game allowed ( 244.2 ), tied for fourth in points per game (18.0), tied for third in EPA per pass (-0.17) and 13th in pressure rate (39.6%), according to Sumer Sports , this season. Also, Macdonald is 6-0 during the regular season against rookie quarterbacks, partly because even veteran signal callers can have a tough time deciphering his defense. But the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner will have some help. Kubiak should be able to prepare him for what type of looks he’ll face on Sunday since Kubiak worked for Macdonald last year as the Seahawks’ offensive coordinator. Additionally, having a unique offensive weapon who can bail quarterbacks out in Brock Bowers, as well as quality check-down options in Michael Mayer and Ashton Jeanty, gives Mendoza a few security blankets to get out of trouble. There’s probably going to be some ups and downs on Sunday — and likely for the rest of the season, for that matter. But if the rookie looks sharp against arguably the best defense in the league this weekend, that should give him a lot of confidence moving forward and bode well for the Raiders’ future. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on how Mendoza looks in his first start. The game kicks off at 1:05 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Twice. That’s the exact amount of times Jaxon Smith-Njigba has been limited to under 100-yards receiving in the nine games the Seattle Seahawks have played this season. With 71 receptions for a league-leading 1,036 yards and nine touchdowns, the 6-foot, 197-pound 24-year-old is arguably the best wideout in the NFL. To say the Las Vegas Raiders defense will have its hands full with Smith-Njigba in Sunday’s Week 10 matchup with the Seahawks this Sunday is an understatement. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard knows JSN presents a supreme challenge for Las Vegas and he expects Seattle to exploit any and all matchups. “Yeah, I mean, he’s unbelievable. He’s number one in the league across the category in all things, receptions,” Leonard said when asked about the collective effort it’ll take to limit Smith-Njigba. “But yeah, it’s very critical. You start with him day one. We’re still talking about him all the way, early down, third down, red zone. Not just coverage-wise, different things that we have to do.” Fully expect the Raiders secondary to get the full JSN experience with cornerbacks Eric Stokes, Darien Porter, Jermod McCoy, Taron Johnson and Hezekiah Masses to get the responsibility of covering the Seahawks elite wide receiver. This is because Seattle isn’t shy about deploying their elite wide receiver in both slot and outside alignments. The 20th pick in the 2023 NFL Draft has been a strong slot receiver since he arrived but he’s spending more time as a perimeter option, too. Now JSN hands out a stiff arm and gets down inside the 10! AZvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JOYUx3HZ6L — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 That slot and boundary capability has truly expanded Smith-Njigba’s effectiveness and the Ohio State product’s production highlights just how much more dangerous he’s become as a weapon in the Seahawks offense. And all this despite Seattle’s offensive attack not being at the level that current Raiders head coach and play caller Klint Kubiak produced when he was the Seahawks offensive coordinator during the team’s Super Bowl-winning run last season. Rookie offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has Seattle’s offense ranked 18th in points scored (202) and yards gained (2,950). The passing game is ranked 17th in yards gained (1,953) and touchdowns scored (15) while the run game is 18th in yards gained (997) and 20th in touchdowns scored (seven). Leonard and the Raiders defense meticulously studying the way the Cardinals covered the Seahawks elite pass catcher in round two of their NFC West contests this year. And one of the defensive tactics Arizona deployed is something Leonard is keen to do with his Las Vegas defense: Zone-heavy and two-high safety looks. While Leonard has deployed more man coverage to try and mitigate defensive woes, returning to a zone-heavy look helps Stokes — who excels in Cover 3 and struggles mightily in man-to-man — and allowed Arizona to bracket Smith-Njigba over the top and took away the deep and intermediate routes where Seattle’s wideout does a lot of his damage. Doing this forced working underneath with shorter passes and this is an area where linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker operate, offering the opportunity to hit JSN — hard. But what a coverage responsibility and experience Smith-Njigba presents to the younger Raiders cornerbacks like Porter, McCoy and Masses. That trio are 25, 21 and 22 years of age, respectively, and going against one of the game’s best wide receivers should be a welcome task, albeit, daunting. Masses has been targeted 31 times allowing 16 receptions (51.6 percent) for 258 yard and a team-leading four touchdowns allowed, while McCoy draws six targets allowing four receptions (66.7 percent) for 63 yards and one touchdown. “Yeah, he’s playing faster. His eyes are in the right spot, and he made a play on the ball, which was awesome,” Leonard said when asked what he’s seen from McCoy this season. “Him and Zeke (Hezekiah Masses) are both growing, and that’s what you’re looking for, is improvement, right? So, it’s been fun to get him more reps so he can feel a little bit more calm out there.” JSN’s elite ability to maintain consistent speed through his routes without telegraphing or slowing down will thoroughly test the entire Raiders secondary’s skillset — beyond the cornerbacks, too. Because Seattle will place their elite pass catcher all over the alignment, even in the backfield and alongside an offensive tackle to truly force the opposing defense’s hand. And if Dean or Walker draw coverage responsibility based on JSN’s alignment and pre-snap motion, good luck, Raiders. At that point, the pass rush and coverage need to combine so disruption of or taking down the quarterback means no dice for Smith-Njigba. Head-to-Head Sunday’s tilt in Allegiant Stadium marks the 57th time the Raiders and Seahawks square off. The Silver & Black lead the all-time series 30-26 (29-25 in regular season play, 1-1 in postseason action). The last time the two teams played one another was in 2022 with Las Vegas dropping Seattle 40-34 in overtime on a walk-off 86-yard run by running back Josh Jacobs. Before that, the Seahawks won the 2018 and 2014 meetings (27-3 and 30-24). Quote of Note “How aggressive you want to be, based on what their personnel is, what our personnel is, and what gives you the best chance of starting fast. Is it coverage? Is it pressure? Is it a different front? There’s a million variables that go into it. And then what personnel package do we want to start with? What 11 do we want to put out there to start the game, and then have a plan to get to a different one later? So those are all factors. How did we practice that week? What was the best thing that we were executing? ‘All right, I like that as a lead call.’ It’s very interactive, both call-wise and personnel-wise, and it’s a week-long conversation of that back-and-forth decision of what’s best.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard on nuances of starting better defensively

teamStories.detailText: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Uchenna Nwosu #7 of the Seattle Seahawks runs across the field during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images A war of attrition remains in the trenches on both sides of the ball for the Seattle Seahawks but at least defensively, there will be slight reinforcements. After missing back-to-back games with an ankle injury, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu practiced in full on Friday and will head into Sunday without an injury designation. The ninth-year pro appeared to be trending toward a return, after consecutive limited practices to start the week, and will now make his return after a full participation on Friday. Nwosu has struggled to stay on the field in recent years, limited to six games in both 2023 and 2024, but has produced for the Seahawks when healthy, posting 9.5 sacks in his debut season in Seattle and seven last year. Through seven games in 2026, the former Charger has just a single sack and a pair of tackles for loss. The Seahawks will need some instant impact from Nwosu, as Leonard Williams remains out with the stinger that saw him leave the game against the Chicago Bears and miss last week’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. While Williams will remain missing form the interior, Brandon Pili will be back in the rotation after recovering from his back injury. Pili practiced in full on Friday after consecutive DNPs to start the week. No such help is headed for Seattle’s offensive line, however, with Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson remaining out with their respective ankle and knee injuries. Cross’s absence is a particular blow, after he was limited in practice on Thursday before a return to DNP status on Friday. Though Sam Darnold remains out as well, backup quarterback Drew Lock will get additional help with the return of Rashid Shaheed, who got in a full week of practice as he has recovered from a knee injury. For the second straight week, Lock was limited in practice across all three days in his ramp up to start, as he continues to manage severe tendinitis , as well as the oblique injury suffered in Week 9 .
